newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan smelters profits seen strong, Mitsui shines.
newsitem.headline: Japan smelters profits seen strong, Mitsui shines.

text.p: Shares in Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co Ltd shine the brightest amongst Japan's six major smelters, which are all expected to post strong profits for the past business year, industry analysts say.
"Mitsui is such a dramatic turn around story," said Stephen Wolfe, analyst at UBS Securities Ltd in Tokyo.
"(Mitsui's) restructuring programme has been very dramatic, and the share prices have not reflected that."

Analysts said Japan's six leading non-ferrous metal refining companies were likely to announce healthy parent current profits for 1996/97 ended March 31, matching their own forecasts of growth between 8.4 percent and 109.0 percent.
Their earnings are due to be announced on May 26.
Current profit is pre-tax profit including gains and losses on non-operating activities such as securities investments.

Analysts ascribe the achievement to the dollar's further advance to above 115 yen from around 108 yen in the first-half of the year, combined with a recovery in the electronics material industry in the second-half of the year.
"A drop of one yen in the dollar's value would bring a profit totalling 110 million yen to the six companies," said Koichi Harie, analyst at Nikko Research Center.
Japan's smelters benefit from the dollar's strength against the yen as their treatment charges are denominated in dollars.
Analysts also said smelters were aided by a double-digit rise in copper treatment charges and a roughly seven percent increase in zinc treatment charges in 1996.
Many analysts recommended buying shares in Mitsui Mining, which has benefitted most from the recovery in the electronics materials sector, through its production of copper foil.

Nikko's Harie noted Mitsui's group price earnings ratio -- which is calculated by dividing the company's earnings per share -- stood at around 20 times, well below those of Sumitomo's 30 times and Mitsubishi's 40 times.
Some also recommend Sumitomo Metal Mining Co Ltd, which owns a gold mine in Kagoshima, southern Japan.
"The gold price fell from $370 per ounce to $340. Its (Sumitomo Metal) shares were sold off quite heavily, yet the currency made up for most of the differences," said UBS' Wolfe.
"About 15 percent of its (Sumitomo Metal's) revenue comes from gold, but (of the 15 percent) the only portion that is exposed to lower-gold prices is five percent," he said.
On the other hand, many analysts reserved judgement on Mitsubishi Materials Corp which they say is struggling in some areas of business, particularly aluminium cans.

While Japan's overall demand for beverage cans is growing, cheap imported aluminium cans are pushing down prices for Japanese products. Some beverage firms are also shifting to using steel cans instead of pricier domestic aluminium cans.
"That's (aluminium cans) still profitable. But they (profits) are shrinking," said Minoru Hasegawa, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts were confident the smelters would see more growth this year -- as long as the dollar does not fall sharply below 115 yen -- helped by expected strength in global metal prices.
"Demand for copper and zinc particularly is fairly strong," UBS's Wolfe said. "(The smelters) are running pretty much at full capacity," he said.

Analysts said 1997 treatment charges for copper were raised marginally. Zinc treatment charges this year were cut by about 10 percent, but the fall should be more than offset by expected strength in zinc prices and an increase in smelters' ratio in price participation clauses with mines, analysts said.
Under the price participation and escalation clauses, smelters' treatment charges fluctuate in accordance with global metal prices.
The six firms forecast the following parent current profits (in billions of yen unless specified):
1996/97 1995/96 yr/yr change
Mitsubishi Materials Corp 9.00 8.30 +8.4 pct
Sumitomo Metal Mining Co 12.00 9.03 +32.9 pct
Mitsui Mining and Smelting 7.60 5.08 +49.6 pct
Dowa Mining Co Ltd 6.00 3.80 +57.9 pct
Furukawa Co Ltd 5.00 4.24 +17.9 pct
Toho Zinc Co Ltd 2.80 1.34 +109.0 pct
